name: CapCut Compound Clip Animation Unlock
use_when: A CapCut sticker, text layer, or graphic layer does not expose the animation controls needed for the edit.
A simple overlay should use video-clip-style animation after its size, rotation, or placement is already set.
The agent needs a mobile-friendly equivalent of nesting or precomposing a graphic so it can be animated as one clip.
A reusable CapCut text animation template should be duplicated while keeping the words editable inside each compound.
Caption or title groups need video effects, such as Player 3 or Blur, applied consistently to grouped text.
avoid_when: A manual position, scale, rotation, opacity, or volume keyframe gives cleaner control.
The original sticker/text needs frequent wording, timing, or layout revisions and compounding would slow iteration.
The compound is being used only to add a flashy preset that does not improve focus, explanation, or tone.

timeline_pattern.pattern: create_or_place_graphic -> set_size_rotation_position -> remove_unneeded_in_out_animation -> create_compound_clip -> apply_video_style_animation -> adjust_duration -> reopen_compound_if_source_changes
timeline_pattern.source_editability_rule: Keep the original layer editable inside the compound so later wording, asset, or timing changes are still possible.
timeline_pattern.template_rule: For repeated animated text lines, build one clean compound, duplicate the compound, then edit words and positions inside each copy instead of rebuilding the animation from scratch.
timeline_pattern.effect_attributes_rule: Apply the effect to one approved compound first, then paste attributes only to matching compounds and review each one against its background.
timeline_pattern.animation_gate_rule: Only compound when the layer type blocks a needed video-clip animation or scene-level transform.
timeline_pattern.qc_rule: Preview the compound at phone size because preset animations can crop, cover captions, or land late after the wrapper is created.

motion.rule: Apply the unlocked animation to the compound only after the graphic's base placement is approved.

keyframe_values.base_setup: Set size, flip, rotation, and starting position before making the compound.
keyframe_values.duration: Short social graphic animations should usually finish before the viewer needs to read the next word or object.
keyframe_values.template_offset: After duplicating compounds, reposition and resize each word so the stack has one primary reading path rather than identical layers fighting for focus.
keyframe_values.cleanup: Remove preset in/out animations from the source layer when the compound animation is meant to own the motion.

sound.rule: Add a pop or whoosh only if the compound animation creates a meaningful entrance, reveal, or exit; keep speech dominant.

captions.rule: Keep ordinary captions outside the compound unless they are intentionally part of the designed graphic.

color.rule: Compound animation should not add blur, glow, or color treatment that makes the graphic slower to read.

implementation.ffmpeg: Model the graphic as a pre-rendered or grouped overlay layer, then animate the wrapper's x/y/scale/opacity while preserving source metadata for revisions.
implementation.remotion: Wrap the sticker/text element in a named Sequence or component, animate the wrapper, and keep the child element editable through props.
implementation.blender: Group the graphic object or use a collection/empty parent so the wrapper can receive animation while the child object stays editable.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Place the sticker/text, set its base look, create a compound clip from it, then apply video-style animation or effect controls to the compound. For repeated animated words, Option-drag or duplicate the compound, double-click to edit the internal text, and reposition each wrapper on the main timeline. For caption compounds, approve one Player 3/Blur/effect treatment first, then paste attributes and QC every phrase.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Nest the graphic or use an After Effects precomp, animate the nest/precomp in Effect Controls, and preserve the source graphic for edits.

common_mistakes: Compounding before the base graphic is placed, which makes later sizing and timing harder.
Forgetting that the compound wrapper can hide the original layer timing unless it is reopened.
Duplicating a compound template but leaving every copy in the same position or with the same word.
Using an unlocked preset animation when manual keyframes would land more accurately.
Pasting compound effects across captions or words without checking each background and phrase length.
Leaving duplicate source animations inside the compound so the graphic moves twice.
Putting captions inside the compound and losing easy caption-safe repositioning.
qc: Was compounding necessary to unlock a needed animation or scene-level transform?
Is the original sticker/text still editable inside the compound?
If the compound is a text template, do duplicated copies have updated words, positions, and hierarchy?
Are duplicate source animations removed or intentionally retained?
Does the compound animation finish before the graphic needs to be read?
If effects were pasted to multiple compounds, did each compound pass readability and contrast review?
Do captions, faces, proof, UI, products, and action remain safe through the compound animation?
